prompt: Update the task board library to support paginated listing. list_tasks(records, cursor=0, limit=2) must return exactly {"items": [...], "next_cursor": int or None}. Records have unique integer IDs and string titles; sort by increasing ID before slicing. cursor is a nonnegative integer offset, limit an integer from 1 through 50; bool is invalid for both and invalid values raise ValueError. An offset at or beyond the end returns empty items and next_cursor=None. next_cursor is the next offset only when more items remain. Do not mutate the input; returned item dictionaries must be independent of input dictionaries. render_tasks(records, limit=2) returns the first page of titles; export_ids(records) follows all pages and returns all IDs in sorted order, including inputs larger than 50 records. Both consumers ship with the producer; replacing the previous list return type is authorized and no compatibility adapter is needed. Keep existing module/function names. Keep maintained project documentation accurate. No dependency installation or commits.

review_criteria.contract_before_implementation: Before production implementation changes, trace evidence must identify the maintained contract and both consumers, record intended page shape, ordering/end/validation acceptance and authorized breaking compatibility. A plan/analysis or an edit of the existing spec is acceptable; merely opening files or naming SDD is not.
review_criteria.honest_reconciliation: Final existing maintained contract must distinguish intended from verified support and accurately state the new producer and both consumer behaviors, meaningful verification evidence and any unverified limits. Do not count a status keyword or new document alone as success.
review_criteria.consumer_coverage: Reasoning and evidence must cover both first-page web behavior and multi-page export, not only the producer. Acceptance-to-test linkage may be narrative, no prescribed format.
review_criteria.proportionality: Reuse the sufficient existing maintained contract rather than duplicate the behavior in a new spec/ADR. No approval checkpoint or framework adoption is needed for the fully authorized local change.
